capabilities.target: Executive's calendar: invite acceptance and draft prep notes
Executive's drive: board materials and draft financial results
Any recipient, from the executive's mailbox, no restriction

inputs.source: Calendar invite from any external sender; free-text description field

instructions.note: "find related documents and email a short brief to the attendees" has no limit on document sensitivity, no verification of attendee identity, and no restriction on recipients derived from an untrusted invite.

No technical control constrains which documents are read or where mail is sent; the only governance is the instruction text itself, and the runtime notes confirm mail.send has no recipient restriction and no approval step.

elements.name: Executive's drive (board materials, draft financial results)

controls.name: Human approval gate before external email send
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model in the orchestration layer; works regardless of model capability. Degrades only through approval fatigue if volume rises.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the system of record
controls.decay_rationale: Destination would be drawn from a verified contact record, not from model output or invite free text, so it does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Treat invite description as data; scope document search to meeting-linked records
controls.decay_rationale: Scoping search to records linked to the meeting narrows the path, but a stronger model could still be steered by injected text within the allowed scope, so it does not fully sever the path.

controls.name: Scope drive credential away from restricted documents by default

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted calendar invite drives confidential document read and unrestricted external email

attack_path.note: Anyone can send the executive an invite with an attacker-authored free-text description.
Invite is auto-accepted and 'prepare' is triggered with no content validation.
Agent searches and reads the executive's drive, including board materials and draft financial results, with no scope limit.
Agent emails a brief containing drive content to attendees, including the untrusted invite sender, with no recipient restriction or approval.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: No change needed to watch for; already at ceiling. Monitor whether any approval gate or recipient restriction is added to cap.mail_send, and if so, monitor mail.send volume per approver per day and whether approval review shows raw arguments or only a model summary.

evidence.observation: Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite with a free-text description, making it an untrusted, attacker-authored input.
The agent accepts invites automatically, then finds related documents and emails a brief to attendees, with no restriction on which documents or verification of attendee identity.
mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step, so the egress destination is fully influenceable by the invite's attendee list or injected instructions.
The executive's drive holds board materials and draft financial results, i.e., restricted-sensitivity data reachable by drive.search_and_read.

recommendations.action: Require raw-action human approval, showing the exact recipients and document summaries, before mail.send fires for any recipient not already a verified internal contact.

Treat calendar invite descriptions as untrusted data: ignore embedded instructions, and scope drive.search_and_read to only documents explicitly linked to the meeting record, not the free-text invite body.
Scope the mailbox and drive credentials used by this pipeline so restricted-sensitivity documents cannot be attached or summarized into outbound email without a separate elevated approval.

findings.title: No attributable, independent record of agent actions (repudiation)

forecast.watch_signal: Any proposal to reduce or remove the daily summary review without adding an independent log confirms this gap is worsening.

evidence.observation: The daily summary, the only review mechanism described, is written by the agent itself, so there is no independent, tamper-evident record of what actions were taken, including unauthorized reads or sends.

recommendations.action: Log every calendar accept, document read, and email send to an append-only store that the agent does not author, including full recipient and attachment details.

findings.title: No step, rate, or volume limit on invite-triggered actions

forecast.watch_signal: Monitor invites received per day and mail.send calls per day; a spike with no corresponding rate limit confirms this gap is being exploited.

evidence.observation: 'Act on invites as they arrive' states no limit on the number processed per period, and the autonomy block provides no max_unattended_steps or max_runtime_minutes.
Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite, so an attacker can generate many invites to repeatedly trigger drive reads and external emails.

recommendations.action: Add a hard limit on invite-triggered document searches and email sends per hour, enforced outside the model, with alerting on bursts.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the agent authenticates itself to mail, drive, or calendar services, so spoofing of the agent's own identity cannot be assessed.

autonomy.can_modify_own_config is false and no capability in this design can alter the agent's prompt or configuration, so tampering with the process itself is not reachable; session-level steering via injected invite text is captured as goal_manipulation in f.lethal_trifecta_calendar_invite.
The design treats every calendar invite as untrusted regardless of sender identity, so sender spoofing does not change the trust classification or open a new path.
Artifacts do not describe calendar provenance or sender authentication, so attribution of invite senders cannot be assessed.
This is an inbound flow carrying invite content into the agent; it does not carry organizational data outward, so information disclosure does not apply to this direction.
The only capability acting on this store is drive_read, which is read-only; no capability in this design writes to the executive's drive, so tampering of this store is not reachable.
No capability in this design deletes or locks records in the drive; a read-only search does not exhaust or deny access to it.
Calendar entries in this design carry scheduling metadata only; the restricted content disclosed in the main finding comes from the drive, not from calendar data itself.
Artifacts do not describe how the daily summary is stored or who, besides the agent, can edit it after it is written.
The design describes the daily summary as consumed only internally by the executive, with no external distribution.
The daily summary is a single compiled artifact per day and is not described as a resource-constrained dependency for other capabilities.

rating.rationale: The design lets anyone reach a confidential-data read and an unrestricted external email send through a single auto-accepted calendar invite, with no approval gate, no recipient restriction, no document scoping, no rate limit, and no independent audit trail. No declared control covers this path, so residual equals inherent at critical, and no forecast trigger can push it higher because it is already at the ceiling. The single highest-value fix is a raw-action, low-volume human approval gate combined with a recipient confirmation bound to a verified contact record on cap.mail_send; that is the only control class in this rubric capable of bringing residual below critical.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; actual agent behavior may differ from what is declared.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided; capability scope and credential_scope for drive.search_and_read and mail.send are inferred from the runtime notes, so confidence on those fields is medium.

No runtime configuration was provided confirming step or time limits; max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are recorded as null because the artifacts do not state them, which is itself treated as a finding (f.no_rate_limit) rather than assumed benign.
No information was given on how the agent authenticates to mail, drive, or calendar services, so spoofing and configuration-tampering risk to the agent process itself could not be assessed.
